notes: Drops over-long GSC search queries as non-keyword text and splits the misleading 'partial' run display. (1) Query-length policy: after trimming, queries longer than 50 Unicode code points are excluded entirely (exactly 50 is kept) from all GSC query datasets (query, query_page, query_country) — never stored as a truncated prefix. This is a shape rule (real keywords do not exceed 50 characters; the production outlier was an 808-character pasted 'role instruction' whose 256-character truncation prefixes had been written into both long-term fact tables), independent of the organization-level PII switch: it applies with privacy filtering off. The rule lives in shared-types (GSC_QUERY_MAX_CHARACTERS + isOverlongGscQuery, code-point based so non-BMP characters are not miscounted) and is enforced centrally in safeGscSnapshots, so collection, publication validation, read paths and both fact-table ingests share one implementation. Snapshots gain an optional excludedQueryRows counter (also on the current manifest; old manifests without it remain readable). It is deliberately NOT a quality flag: dropping non-keyword rows never marks a run partial, and pagination.rowsReturned keeps Google's raw count. The publication validator now requires the row gap to be fully explained: rowsReturned - rows.length - excludedQueryRows must be 0, or the remainder must still be explained by the existing PII/URL/invalid quality reasons — a positive count alone never excuses an arbitrary mismatch, and corrupted counts (negative or non-integer) are normalized away rather than passed through. Both ingests drop their 256-character query truncation branch (page/country/device truncation flags remain); /growth-terms and /growth-dimensions filter legacy 256-character prefixes out at read time, so old derived rows stop appearing in lists and CSVs immediately. Growth insights add an info notice disclosing that query detail excludes over-long text while totals keep Google's original aggregates. GA4 dimensions, GSC totals, URL page-identity rules, and the single-site audit's independent GSC path are intentionally untouched. (2) Run display split: backend run.status and quality gates are unchanged; a new pure front-end classifier (apps/web/lib/growthRunDisplay.ts) shows '抓取完成，有后处理告警' when a partial run has every requested source succeeded and all quality reasons are in an explicit post-processing allowlist (search_terms_truncated, dimension_facts_truncated, search_terms_ingest_failed, dimension_facts_ingest_failed — the long-term libraries are read-only projections; their failures do not lose Google data). Everything else (missing days, sampling, thresholding, PII/URL markers, row caps, unknown reasons) fail-closed to the original '部分完成' wording, and retry buttons now appear only for sources that actually failed to collect. (3) A one-shot cleanup script (apps/api/scripts/cleanup-gsc-overlong-queries.mts) deletes the legacy 256-character prefix rows from the two fact tables; it defaults to dry-run, never prints query text, and --commit requires organization, site, the 256-prefix sha256 fingerprint and per-table expected counts, aborting with a rolled-back transaction on any mismatch. It touches only the derived fact rows — disk snapshots, manifests, runs and historical reports are untouched; it is run after this release reaches production. Known boundary: rolling back to an older writer and re-collecting would re-write the prefixes; re-run the script then. Local verification: three-package typecheck, pnpm --filter api test (1433 passed / 34 skipped, +16), web production build, a new browser regression for the run-display split (desktop 1440 / mobile 375: three-state badges, summary recount, no retry button for post-processing-only runs, no overflow, no page errors), and re-runs of the growth-terms, growth-dimensions and org-privacy-setting browser regressions. No SQL migration and no schema change. Rollback to v0.2.21 is compatible and is the declared rollback target.
